request.state:
Evaluate a hypothetical company's prospective product-value decision; you are a classifier, not a researcher or an actual customer. Assume the Can product is implemented according to its stated runtime/storage/UI/MCP contracts. Today's lack of compiler/libraries/infrastructure is the declared design stage and cannot count against merit. Actual draft omissions and support uncertainty remain relevant. No execution, customer demand or willingness to pay has been measured. Source facts are from baseline-20261004T041647Z/snapshot, with independently saved audit evidence.

P is a 25-person professional-services firm with 3 departments, 500 ordinary equipment requests, 80 private expenses/month and 2,000 existing receipt files/records. Employees use browser or authorized chatbot, an operations lead owns policy, finance owns reimbursement evidence and a contracted steward owns installation/updates/incidents. Staff do not program. Required outcomes include owner-private requests, current departmental manager reads, version conflicts, authorized CSV intake/export, immutable claims, distinct eligible reviewers, correction history and truthful reimbursement. Bank payment, accounting/payroll and normal email remain external. Can's pinned team/auth/D1/UI/MCP defaults and owning operation interfaces can express these outcomes without payment/email providers for the small register; independently authored Can and Django drafts covered eight register paths under disclosed DIFFERENT privacy/duplicate/limit choices. They do not prove equal-behavior token superiority or total-task cost. Both later constrained-field changes block an overlong archived title under inherited immutable history; explicit old-evidence policy is required, not a Can-only limitation. Baseline CanExpense submission can name an active colleague who lacks reviewer role, then locks reassignment; narrow eligibility/revocation recovery needs correction. Reviewer recognition/directory disclosure is unresolved, not proved unusable. A later >EUR500 second-approval edit expresses the production rule but cannot supply a valid successful inline example needing three distinct same-team accounts under the current two-account test contract; narrow test-identity clarification is needed.

W is a two-location workspace operator with 12 staff,120 customer organizations,600 members,30 rooms,100 pooled desks; monthly work is 3,000 bookings,500 invoices,300 physical mail items and30,000 notices. The director owns customer continuity, an external steward provides technical support, and customer administrators/members use limited portal grants. REQUIRED suite replacement spans shared customer identity/records, proposals/reservations/invoice collection, membership/reception/mail, scoped reports, data migration and coordinated recovery. Several Can apps may compose ONE solution in ONE deployment; unused suite features are irrelevant. Only genuinely cancellable suite charges count ONCE. Accounting/payroll, processor, email/domain, physical-access vendor and necessary support remain. Selected commercial/mail source paths provide explicit scopes, immutable terms, delivered-versus-paid distinctions and retries. Concrete draft corrections remain: 101 eligible hold-cleanup rows cannot drain an all-or-nothing limit100 scan; live verification invariant blocks normal stored-delegate revocation; Report accepts fresh+incomplete checkpoints that can look like zero. Mail's optional no-fee/manual-evidence variant still pulls invoice/membership providers through whole-owner closure. Full ResourcePolicy snapshots copy retained booking arrays repeatedly; sequential B retained bookings imply B(B+1)/2 logical embedded values (5,050 at100;500,500 at1000), not measured bytes/latency/bill. Coalescing removes only an in-transaction factor; narrower immutable facts require exact historical reconstruction. Proposed remedies reuse current predicates/admission/typed per-record work/completeness checks; equal-outcome source and cost evidence has not established the optional partition or history alternative. Wider membership/reception and historical intake remain acceptance conditions, not omitted obligations. Canonical CSV does not by itself ingest prior locked evidence and receipt files; a bounded steward mapping or retained read-only archive is needed and priced. The handwritten CanRent desired JavaScript target passes accumulated minor units to a major-unit money constructor and bypasses checked-money helpers in some operations; correct target correspondence, while valid source-authored minor-integer projections remain legitimate. No generated-code or executed amount error is asserted.

S is a 40-person maintenance contractor,15 field staff,200 jobs/week,5,000 assets. Inspections, assignments, stock receipt and scoped reports fit record workflows, but essential offline maps and fleet route optimization are outside Can's CRUD-first scope. Full field-suite cancellation is therefore unsupported. A partial module must retain the route/offline subscription and integrate source identity/recovery; no subscription saving or staff-time gain for that module has been measured.

All economics are HYPOTHETICAL USD scenario inputs over24 future months, not vendor quotes or engineering estimates. P truly avoidable incumbent bill is assumed450/month: low-support incremental Can setup740,monthly difference40,1month overlap ->8,650 net savings; high-support2420,355,2months -> -1,040. W assumed900/month avoidable: low5220,150,2months ->10,980; high15140,1015,4months -> -21,500. Recurring differences count steward/staff effort, nonzero shared-platform funding and incremental providers on BOTH sides. Technical rate100/h and staff35/h; Can steward P1-4h/month/W4-12h/month. Shared platform charges and setup/migration/training/overlap are not free; incumbent future configuration/support also costs. C's current primary provider tariffs give $5 shared Workers minimum plus W $9.45 email overage at30k notices =14.45/month BEFORE other usage/payment/domains/backup/platform/support; sending is Beta and quota/domain approval conditional. Do not multiply minimums or savings by module count. D1 Time Travel30days Paid restores database only; code rollback/R2 do not provide full composed recovery. Clarify existing fenced install/upgrade/restore plan and config-only provider swap retention of old receipt namespace, never undo external money by restoring a database. Residency/recovery objectives/company security policy require buyer validation; no compliance claim.

Choose NEXT allocation under this prospective scenario from three comparable strategies: retain/configure the existing tools with no Can investment now; fund a limited future Can validation pilot without a replacement commitment; or commit budget to a complete composed replacement programme, with actual switch only after unchanged required workflows/costs/recovery pass. A future bounded validation would have unquoted NONZERO steward/staff/provider/setup cost plus retained subscriptions, and may not be worthwhile. Obtain a quote and spending cap before authorizing work. P would examine isolated register+expense decision review, W shadow commercial/mail/report evidence without customer cutover, S separate inspection records while keeping offline routing. No cheap pilot allowance or complete-delivery price is assumed. Evaluate usefulness, full required coverage, ownership/support, credible incumbent configuration, switching/data continuity, uncertain savings and evidence strength equally. Do not infer market adoption from your classifications.

P.instructions: Which next investment strategy best fits P under the given conditional capabilities, $450 avoidable bill and low/high support scenarios?

criteria.retain: Keep/configure incumbent tools now; allocate no Can effort or pilot funds in this decision.
criteria.pilot: Seek a quote/cap for only the bounded future P validation to validate outcomes/review/cost; retain subscriptions and do not commit to replacement.
criteria.replace: Commit a composed P replacement programme budget now, accepting the stated correction/support uncertainty; cut over only after all original required outcomes and economics pass.

W.instructions: For W, choose the strongest next allocation given complete suite outcomes, $900 avoidable fee, unresolved source corrections and cost sensitivity.

criteria.retain: Continue incumbent configuration with no Can allocation now, preserving existing continuity and subscription burden.
criteria.pilot: Fund only the bounded shadow W pilot after narrow corrections to test whole-path/report/support assumptions; no customer cutover or replacement commitment.
criteria.replace: Authorize the complete composed W replacement programme now, with retained services/corrections and gated cutover only once every original required workflow, data and recovery criterion passes.

S.instructions: For S, which next strategy is justified when essential offline/routing remains outside Can and partial-module economics are unknown?

criteria.retain: Maintain/configure the existing field suite; do not invest in Can at this point.
criteria.pilot: Limit investment to the future isolated inspection-record pilot while retaining offline/routing tools; no full-suite savings or replacement commitment.
criteria.replace: Commit to a partial Can inspection/record replacement programme now with offline/routing subscription retained and migration/support/acceptance gates, acknowledging no quantified avoidable bill or labor gain.
